x: Twenty-years old John Dear, who has been running for little more than twelve months, illustrated his rapid improvement by winning this year's Yacht '3' from a mark of 2min-10secs.
So there is plenty of scope you youngsters for gaining some glory! John Dear(a useful prospect), Mike Shingles and Fred Paget were the only others to show noticeably good form.

Special mention must be made of John Dear,who backed up the 'A'team so well and was unlucky to go without a medal. Incidentally the two Johns - Dear and Thresher - were held up in a traffic jam at Rochester Bridge on their way to the race and did most of their warm-up by running a mile to the changi…

Bicourt and Hart were always well placed, with Mike Shingles making ground close behind. Dave Cocks and Pete Sadler disappointed and it was left to John Dear to complete our scoring four after a fine run in 59th place.

Perhaps those runners who fail to answer cards will substitute courtesy for generosity in 1965 - perhaps. Those who did what they could to salvage the situation were Trevor Hart (13th), Tony Fairclough (29th) and John Dear (49th).
Tony Fairclough and John Dear got a very good start but the latter paid dearly(!) for his effort and went back steadily down the field to a below-form 102nd.

John Dear, who started fast, fell back a little but still finished 19th. Charlie Smart (still going very strongly at the age of 55!), Gordon Biscoe, Don Maclean (one of his off days), George Piddington and Chris Keavey completed our two teams.
Jack Brown also ran well and will no doubt be picking up many Vets prizes come his 40th birthday in August. John Dear,Don Maclean and the "Dukes Joggers" completed our two teams. 153 finished.

John Dear passed Mitcham on stage 8 but had to allow Poly to pass. We were still 4th, 1½mins behind the second team and 28secs behind the third--Blackheath were certain winners and the race was on for second place.

On the second stage Gerry North opened the gap to about fifty seconds and John Dear held on to 3rd place for the B team. Trevor Hart ran the third stage for the A team and widened the gap over the Manchester club to about 80 seconds but Bolton United who had had a bad start had moved into 3rd place…

The 3000m Steeplechase (a new championship event which should become more popular) proved an easy victory for John Bicourt whose experience at this type of race was too much for John Dear who had led in the early stages .

Some really hard work was put in by John Thresher in the 'half' and in stopping the watches at 1:54.9 he made some amends for his defeat in the Club Champs by 'you know who' . Other noteworthy times were Mel Thorpe's 4:16.2 in the mile (best for some years) and John Dear's 4:25.0 (best ever).

All this year John Dear has been hovering around 10 minutes for the 3000m Steeplechase,but at last he has broken through, He started steadily working his way up the field until with three laps to go he found himself in the lead.
The relay started with our two representatives Charlie Walker and John Dear lining up with 24 other teams. Both ran somewhat below themselves to bring the 'A' team in 18th and the 'B' team 17th.
The end of the day was greeted with the satisfaction and knowledge that we had completed one of the toughest days training we are likely to attempt, at least until next year! John Dear

John Dear improved on his disappointing run in the previous week's South of Thames race with a well placed 36th. Charlie Walker, who had plenty to say during the race---(it must demoralise the opposition) was our third scorer.
Although my subjects are a little older than this, and you may need to watch for rather more than one season, I would commend to my favoured clients the following promising specimens:-John Dear.
John Dear was well in the lead at one point, but unfortunately he went off course, leaving John Thresher to stroll round for a leisurely win.

These two prepared the foundation for a winning score and it only needed John Bicourt and John Dear to finish 30th and 40th respectively for us to clinch a win---positions they would normally achieve quite comfortably; Bicourt being 21st last year.
…hern Championships in February. Mel Thorpe, recent runner-up in the South of Thames Junior, took 2nd handicap prize and John Dear 3rd.…

Joe Reilly was starting to make some impression after a slowish start and Howard Satchell, who was originally only reserve, had dispatched Chris Keavey etc. and for a few glorious miles had his sights trained on Ranjit Bhatia and John Dear.

Held on the same day as the Inter-Counties Championship at Blackpool, this third league match found us with our points lead in jeopardy, as Gerry and Geoff North, John Thresher, Tony Fairclough and Trevor Hart were on call by their Counties and Mel Thorpe, Alan Black, and John Dear were also away.
Bill Dance was 2nd in exactly 10 minutes with John Dear close behind. Another solo effort for a record was John Thresher's very even paced mile of 4:13.2 .

Farther back John Dear was sticking on John Bicourt's tail as they strove to regain contact with the leading quartet. With two laps to go Joe had dropped and only Alan and Adrian were left in the championship battle,and at 660 yds the former struck out for home, opening up his winning margin of 15 y…

It was at 3-15 pm that Bill Lucas sent over 300 runners on their way over the 5 mile course at Sparrows Den, West Wickham, and it was with some suprise that after a small lap of 1 mile Brian Buxton was seen to be leading the field followed closely by Bill Dance, Mel Thorpe, Adrian Major and John Dear.
(Photo by Stanley Devon) The ruck of the G.L.C. field splash past the mile mark at Parliament Hill, with John Dear (16) and Bill Kerr (17) in the thick of it.
Laurie O'Hara was very unhappy with the going and his 20th position, although creditable, belied his true form. John Dear finished 36th and Bill Kerr 41st, but Cadogan could not close in a team.

Blackheath and Ranelagh were almost at full strength yet only managed to beat our restricted team by 46 points and 6 points respectively. John Dear (left) and Howard Satchell plough their way through the mud with only 1½ miles gone.
Fairclough was 35th, not at all happy, but John Dear who ran only because of Alan Black's last minute withdrawal, was running the race of his life in 59th spot.
John Dear turned in another good performance, considering the company, to complete our scoring team, it being unfortunate that Gerry Williams arrived too late to be declared.
Howard Satchell set off as though deputising for Gerry North but paid dearly for the experience and it was left to Chris Steer and John Dear to lead our men home in 3rd and 6th places respectively.

John Dear did everything that was asked of him as reserve but our long stage men found the opposition too much to cope with. There were plenty of "ifs" and "buts" floating around after the race but great teams win despite their set-backs and Coventry had more of these than anyone!
STAGE 4: John Dear (17:22 - 13th fastest) John was in the unenviable position of being a last minute replacement for Gerry Williams and taking over in 4th place.

The most inspiring event of the afternoon was the 3000m Steeplechase, won by John Dear, but with the amazing Don Maclean only 16 seconds down in 2nd place and beating all the other clubs' 'A' runners., a tremendous feat by our hard working Press Secretary.
On the track John Dear recorded a good 9:37.8 for 4th in the Steeplechase and Peter Hilliar made a welcome return to our trophy team with 3rd in the 'B' 880y.
With Pat Newell, John Dear, and Lionel Mann (amongst others) also waiting for an opportunity to nip in I would say the position of every runner is precarious to say the least.
JOHN BICOURT (top) leads Lightfoot (Devonport) and goes on to beat the Devon man by 6 yds, finishing 2nd in 9:05.8, whilst JOHN DEAR (bottom) takes a dive but recovered well to finish 6th in 9:42.0.
Dick Piotrowski held second place and although John Dear dropped to 6th on stage three they were still ahead of the 'A' outfit despite fine recovery efforts by Bill Dance and Gerry North.

John Dear had come into the team at short notice - he is making a habit of this - and although running steadily had to concede three places and at the end of the fourth leg we were back to 6th and were 80 secs down on Derby who were still the leaders.

Having won this race last year it was necessary this time to find a completely new team and with Dick Piotrowski, John Dear, Roger Donnison, Lionel Mann, Malcolm Simms, Howard Satchell, Bob Glover and Pat O'Connor eligible we appeared to have a strong team but unfortunately Donnison, Mann, Simms and…

The move through the field must begin; but as Bill Dance (48), John Dear (53) and Whewell made ground slowly so our leading two lost it and 5½ miles later our final points score was six greater at 186.
Things were now hotting up and at the bottom of Copse, Hart, O'Hara, Bicourt and Major had broken away from Bill Dance with Bill Kerr and John Dear close up and the rest strung out in single file.
John Dear (14:51 - 8th fastest) For several years John has been destined to serve as a regular reserve in our teams, so it was good to see him gaining his place this time as a first choice.
John Bicourt looks favourite, but just how far behind him John Dear, Bill Dance and Dick Piotrowski are when it comes to selection remains to be seen.

A fine run by John Dear in the steeplechase and a promising 440 by Jim Vivian on the last leg of the medly relay were also noteworthy, but the finest performance of the afternoon was undoubtedly the 6'-0" high jump of our junior, Arnold Bent.

…Thresher and Major ... pulled out for a pit stop just after the line - yes, he's out for good - transmission has gone - John Dear ... on the line Davies has gone in front of Merry and Piddington who are hanging on grimly ... at the front the four leaders are drawing steadily away from the field led…

Last year's steeplechase result was reversed when John Dear just held off the Dance finish to score a popular win. (Our 8:52.0 chaser, John Bicourt, opted for the mile, as did our sub 9:20 man Alan Black.) Perhaps some of the massive mile field would surprise themselves if they tackled this event next year.

Our second claim long jumper Alan Lerwill took his speciality with a leap of 22'-8¾", but John Dear had an unhappy outing in the steeplechase with his season's slowest of 10:04---neverless he still got a bronze for his effort!
Nick Head did season's bests in Javelin and Shot, as did Tony Brooks in his heat of the 800 metres. Jim Vivian finished 5th in the 200 metres final and John Dear 4th in steeplechase (9:51.6).

John Dear on Stage 8 had to contend with Grant of Coventry and at one stage it looked as if the Coventry runner would gain a large lead but John recovered well from a bad patch and in the end was only 8 seconds behind.

It was a sight for sore eyes to see five Belgrave vests well placed after the first mile and although John Dear, one of the five, was forced to fall back the claret and gold of the remaining four kept well to the fore right to the end.
However, it was very encouraging to see both John Bicourt and John Dear running so well in top class company on the road, where their attention has not hitherto been diverted.
Not far behind, in one of his best ever road runs was John Dear a full minute clear of Kelly Diprose and Bill Kerr---both only recently back in training again.

John Dear looked impressive and was only 30 seconds down on Laurie O'Hara with a lap to go. Robert Cross had his first outing since joining us, but has yet to reach racing fitness.
Patrick O'Connor, Lionel Mann and John Dear ran well and Tony Brien in his first major race for us showed he is a new member with considerable promise.
He made an impact last December when he finished up amongst our senior first team men in the Club '7', taking the handicap as well, and beating John Dear and Dick Piotrowski.

With Dick Piotrowski and Alan Black also well under 10 minutes and John Dear , recovered from a nasty injury, capable of 9-30 or under, we look strong.

And so they remained, until 3,000 metres when Lionel Mann dropped off the back, followed two laps later by Laurie O'Hara and John Dear. The medal winners had thus emerged and Morris looked by far the most comfortable.

…Pat O'Connor and Lionel Mann; Charlie Dabbs and Alan Black both showing new leases of life that shouldn't be underated; John Dear, whose current form will beat more than one of those already mentioned and, finally, Bob Cross whom we look forward to seeing again after his summer season in Achilles co…
With two laps complete it was Mann (28:37) setting the pace from Major, both 10 yards clear of Fairclough with John Dear running the race of his life another 50 yards back.
In contrast, John Dear found his first National a struggle and looked unhappy from the beginning. He finished just one place behind former team-mate Mel Thorpe who was Coventry's 7th man.

John Dear showed his potential this winter when he finished twelfth in the "Middlesex", ahead of Laurie O'Hara. He is much stronger than in previous years and I expect him to produce a run of best ever times during March and April.

John Dear was 12 secs faster than 'A' man Lionel and they finished almost together in 4th and 6th places. Gerry ("my legs didn't belong to me") held his position but made no ground, while Clive dropped the 'B' team from 6th to 11th.
